Go mobile with this offline PDF map viewer. Pinpoints your current location on PDF maps from the Hunting Atlas, Fishing Atlas, CPW Maps Library, or any georeferenced PDF. No need for internet or cell tower connection! Plus, access a list of resources for downloading PDF maps.

The Imported Maps page contains all the maps that you have downloaded and imported. These maps are copied into this app\'s data folder so that the map data is still available to use when you go mobile. Each imported map displays: the map name, file size, and current distance from the map in miles. See Add Map, Edit Map, and View Map sections below to add, rename, delete, or view a map.
If you are on the map, the location icon, pictured above, will be displayed.
Click on the + button on the Imported Maps page to download or import a map.
Click on a map to display the map, view current location, zoom in or out, and add waypoints.
Long press on a map to change the map name, delete the map, or view it\'s file size and latitude, longitude boundaries.

Click on the Open Browser button to download a map. Note that this requires an internet connection. It will notify you that it is starting up your browser app. Then it will load a page from the CPW website with resources to download georeferenced PDFs. Scroll down to the CPW Mobile PDF section to see these resources. Use one of the resources described below to download a map. If you have changed the default app that displays PDFs and that app does not allow saving the map, reset the default PDF viewer in Settings/Apps.
Click on \'CPW online Map Library\'. Click on show 2 filters to display GISFileType filter. Set this to GeoPDF. Click the download icon for the desired map.

Click on \'Colorado Hunting Atlas\' or \'Fishing Atlas\'. Select your map layers by tapping on the menu icon in the top-left. Set your zoom level. Then press the down arrow icon. It will allow you to change: map scale, map size, and orientation. Smaller map scales will show more detail. Larger map sizes will show larger map areas. Enter a PDF file name and press the Create PDF button. Wait for it to be created and then press Download PDF.

Click on \'USFS\'. Search for a location. When the forest service individual map boundaries are showing, click on one of the rectangles. Then in the popup box, click the \'>\' icon. Lastly, click on \'Download PDF\'.

Click on \'USGS\'. Search for a location and tap on it. Scroll down to the most recent map and tap on it. Scroll down and select GeoPDF. It may download immediately. If it does not, wait for it to display, click on the menu icon, and then click on \'download\' or \'save\'.

After you have downloaded PDF maps *go back to this app and import them by tapping on the File Picker button. Use the menu in the top-left to select from Recent, Documents, or Downloads folders. Or select the Google Drive icon if the file is located there. Tap on the PDF file, and it will import it and display the map. The map file is copied to the app directory so deleting the original will not affect the imported maps.
* Hint to get back to this app: tap the back icon next to the home icon at the bottom of your phone.

Location:
Your current latitude and longitude will be displayed at the top of the map, and it will be displayed on the map as a cyan circle outlined in white.

Viewing the Map:
Double tap or pinch to zoom in or out. Drag to pan the map.

Waypoints:
To add waypoints, tap on the pushpin icon at the top-right, then tap the map at the desired location. To cancel adding a waypoint, tap again on the pushpin icon. If the waypoint label is showing, tapping elsewhere on the map will hide it. Tapping on a waypoint will display it's label and edit, move, and delete buttons. Edit will let you edit the label and pushpin color. It will display the date added and the latitude, longitude. Move will turn the pin gray and display a bullseye icon. Zoom or pan the bullseye icon to the desired location. Then tap MOVE HERE, located at the top of the screen, to move the waypoint. The delete button will delete the waypoint.

Tracks:
To add tracks, tap on the path icon at the top right. It will begin tracing your current track. It will adjust the interval that it checks your location by how fast you are traveling. If you are walking or standing still it checks every 15 seconds. If running, every 5 seconds. If driving, every 2 seconds. To stop tracking, tap on the path icon again. Tapping on a track will show it's label and an edit and delete button. You can edit the color and label.

KMZ Files:
You can download or upload a KMZ file of your tracks and waypoints in the dropdown menu.

Loading Adjacent Maps:
Shows a list of nearby maps. This is useful to quickly switch to a new map if you are going off the edge of the current map. Tapping the Load Adjacent Maps button will let you pick a map to switch to. This feature can be turned on or off in the App Settings user preferences. If you have tracking turned on and you switch maps, it will start a new track for that map.

User Preferences:
Settings that remain the same for all maps are found under App Settings. Note that when showing waypoints is turned off, adding a waypoint will temporarily show all waypoints. Settings that are specific to each map are found under Map Settings. The setting for locking the map in landscape or portrait is useful if you are driving on a 4-wheel-drive road and the map switches orientation with each bump!
